title: Forms with React Hook Form + Zod
readme:
Full-Stack Developer 2026 - Phase 21
Forms with React Hook Form + Zod

This phase continues Volume 06 after Phase 20 Production Application UI. It adds professional create/edit forms while preserving NestJS as the authoritative validation, authorization and business-rule boundary.

Use 13_Phase_21_Complete_Book.pdf for continuous reading, or the numbered focused PDFs for targeted study.

lessons.title: Form State and Submission Mental Model
lessons.summary: Form State & Submission Mental Model Understand what a form owns before installing a form library Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod Volume 06 - Professional Frontend A form is a temporary editing workspace A form is not the database record…
lessons.body:
Form State & Submission Mental
Model
Understand what a form owns before installing a form library

Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

A form is a temporary editing workspace
A form is not the database record itself. It is a temporary client-side editing model that collects user
intent. Until the server accepts the request, the form contains proposed data, not authoritative
application state.

FORM STATE                                                SERVER STATE

typed title                                                stored Task

selected priority                                            authorization

dirty fields                                              business rules

client errors                                          database constraints
Figure 1 - Form state and authoritative server state have different owners.

The lifecycle

User edits fields

React Hook Form tracks values, touched/dirty state and errors

Zod validates the client-side form shape

Submit maps form values to API input

NestJS validates the request again

Business rules and authorization run

Prisma persists accepted state

UI refreshes from authoritative server result

Why not plain useState for every field?
You can build forms with useState, but large forms quickly accumulate repetitive value, touched, error,
reset and pending logic. React Hook Form provides a focused form-state model and works especially
well with native uncontrolled inputs.

What stays local?
State                                Best owner

Input values                         React Hook Form

Touched / dirty / field errors       React Hook Form

Reusable validation rules            Zod

Authoritative Task list              Server / later TanStack Query

Authorization                        NestJS

Business rules                       NestJS service

Persistent constraints               PostgreSQL

Anti-pattern

Do not put every form keystroke into a global store or TanStack Query cache. Form state is inherently local and
transient.

lessons.title: Accessible Fields Errors and Validation UX
lessons.summary: Accessible Fields, Errors & Validation UX Make forms understandable to keyboard, screen-reader and sighted users Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod Volume 06 - Professional Frontend A form field is more than an input A production field needs a visible label,…
lessons.body:
Accessible Fields, Errors & Validation UX Make forms understandable to keyboard, screen-reader and sighted users Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod Volume 06 - Professional Frontend A form field is more than an input A production field needs a visible label, optional help text, an input control, and an error relationship that assistive technology can understand.
{errors.title ? (

{errors.title.message}

) : null}
Error UX rules Show errors next to the relevant field, use human language, preserve the user's input, and move focus or provide a summary when a large form fails in a way that would otherwise be difficult to discover. Do Avoid Visible Placeholder as the only label aria-invalid on invalid fields Color-only error indication aria-describedby to the error Unrelated error text with no relationship role="alert" for newly appearing concise errors Dozens of noisy live regions Keep focus behavior predictable Automatically moving focus after every keystroke Client validation timing TaskFlow uses mode: "onBlur" for most field validation: the user can type without constant interruption, then receives feedback after leaving a field. Submission still validates everything. Server remains authoritative A perfect client form does not secure an API. A caller can bypass the browser completely. NestJS must validate the transport request again.

lessons.title: Edit Forms Reset Dirty and Default Values
lessons.summary: Edit Forms, Reset, Dirty State & Defaults Model the difference between loaded data, unsaved edits and saved server state Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod Volume 06 - Professional Frontend Edit forms begin with authoritative defaults An edit form should receive…
lessons.body:
Edit Forms, Reset, Dirty State &
Defaults
Model the difference between loaded data, unsaved edits and saved server state

Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Edit forms begin with authoritative defaults
An edit form should receive values derived from the server record, not independently refetch the same
Task just because the form is a Client Component.

Server Component loads authorized Task

Convert Task -> TaskFormValues

Render <TaskForm defaultValues=...>

React Hook Form tracks edits locally

Dirty state
isDirty answers whether current form values differ from the form's defaults. That enables a useful Save
button and unsaved-change messaging without manually comparing every field.

const {
formState: { isDirty, isSubmitting },
} = useForm<TaskFormValues>({
resolver: zodResolver(taskFormSchema),
defaultValues,
});

<button disabled={!isDirty || isSubmitting}>
Save changes
</button>

Reset after a successful save
After the server accepts updated values, reset the form to the accepted representation. That tells
React Hook Form that the saved values are now the baseline and clears dirty state.

const saved = await updateTaskFromBrowser(taskId, input);

const nextDefaults = taskToFormValues(saved);
reset(nextDefaults);

When initial record identity changes

React Hook Form reads defaultValues as initialization. If the same mounted form starts editing another
Task, explicitly call reset(newValues), or key the form by Task ID so React remounts it.

Do not use reset as data fetching

reset() changes local form state. It does not fetch or prove server freshness. The server remains the source of
truth.

lessons.title: Nullable Optional Date Select and Coercion Rules
lessons.summary: Nullable, Optional, Dates, Selects & Coercion Translate browser-native values into deliberate API semantics Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod Volume 06 - Professional Frontend Optional, nullable and empty are different Representation Meaning field omitted Caller is not sending this property null…
lessons.body:
Nullable, Optional, Dates, Selects
& Coercion
Translate browser-native values into deliberate API semantics

Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Optional, nullable and empty are different
Representation                    Meaning

field omitted                     Caller is not sending this property

null                              Caller explicitly clears the value

""                                UI string is currently empty

undefined                         JavaScript property/value is absent

HTML inputs naturally produce strings, so the form layer often needs to translate empty strings into null
or omitted transport properties.

Description
description: values.description.trim()
? values.description.trim()
: null,

datetime-local
The browser's datetime-local control does not include a timezone offset. TaskFlow treats the entered
wall-clock value as the user's local time, converts it to a JavaScript Date, and then sends an ISO
timestamp to the API.

dueAt: values.dueAtLocal
? new Date(values.dueAtLocal).toISOString()
: null,

Time-zone warning

For systems where the intended time zone can differ from the browser zone, add an explicit time-zone field or
domain rule. Do not assume datetime-local is globally unambiguous.

Selects and enums
<select {...register("priority")}>
<option value="LOW">Low</option>
<option value="MEDIUM">Medium</option>
<option value="HIGH">High</option>
</select>

Numbers and coercion

HTML number inputs also produce strings unless you opt into conversion. Use RHF options such as
valueAsNumber when appropriate, or transform at the form boundary. Avoid hidden coercion for
identifiers and security-sensitive values.

lessons.title: Submission Pending Server Errors and Duplicate Submits
lessons.summary: Submission, Pending State & Server Errors Handle asynchronous failures without losing user input Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod Volume 06 - Professional Frontend Client validation is only the first failure layer Form field error - fix locally Network failure -…
lessons.body:
Submission, Pending State &
Server Errors
Handle asynchronous failures without losing user input

Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Client validation is only the first failure layer
Form field error - fix locally

Network failure - no HTTP response

401 - session/token recovery

403 - authenticated but not allowed

409 / business conflict - explain operation conflict

500 - generic safe message + requestId

Root server error
setError("root.server", {
type: "server",
message: "Unable to save this task.",
});

Field-level server error
If the API returns a structured error that clearly belongs to one field, map it back with
setError("fieldName", ...). Do not guess based on message text. Prefer stable API error codes or
structured validation details.

Keep the form after failure
Do not erase the form because the server returned 409 or the network disconnected. Preserve the
user's work and let them correct or retry.

Duplicate-submit protection

A disabled submit button prevents accidental double clicks in the browser, but it is not a distributed
idempotency guarantee. Payments and other sensitive operations may need a server-side idempotency
strategy later.

Error contract reuse

Phase 13 gave TaskFlow stable error codes and request IDs. Phase 21 consumes that contract rather than
creating a second frontend-only error language.

lessons.body:
Controller & Custom Components
Know when native registration ends and an adapter is justified

Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Prefer register for native inputs
React Hook Form works naturally with native input, textarea and select elements. Start with register.
Use Controller/useController only when a component is controlled by design or does not expose a
standard input ref/value contract.

register                                   Controller

input                                     date picker

textarea                                    rich select

select                                custom combobox

checkbox                               third-party UI control

Controller pattern
<Controller
name="assigneeId"
control={control}
render={({ field, fieldState }) => (
<AssigneeCombobox
value={field.value}
onChange={field.onChange}
onBlur={field.onBlur}
error={fieldState.error?.message}
/>
)}
/>

Do not wrap everything in Controller
Controller adds an adapter layer. Native controls already integrate well through register and are
usually simpler and more accessible. Reach for Controller when the component API requires it, not
because a form library example happened to use it.

Reusable form-field components
A reusable Field component can own label/help/error layout, but avoid hiding register/control behavior
behind a component so generic that no one can understand where values and errors come from.

lessons.body:
Shared Validator Package &
Boundaries
Extract only validation concepts with a real second consumer

Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Now a shared package has earned its place
In Phase 12 we deliberately kept API schemas in the API because the frontend did not yet need them.
Phase 21 introduces a real second consumer. This is the moment when a small validators workspace
package becomes justified.

packages/validators/
package.json
src/
tasks.ts
index.ts

apps/api/
imports shared field rules into transport schemas

apps/web/
imports shared field rules into form schemas

What belongs in the package?
Good shared candidates                              Keep app-specific

Title/description field rules                       Browser-only form layout

Transport-neutral enums                             NestJS exceptions

Reusable Zod primitives                             Prisma client

Cross-app DTO schema when truly identical           Next.js routing

Small type exports derived from schemas             Database service logic

Avoid a shared junk drawer
Do not turn packages/validators into packages/shared-everything. Every export should be
transport-neutral or validation-focused.

Form schema can still be web-specific
The shared package does not force the browser form to mirror the HTTP body. The web can compose
shared field rules into a UI-specific schema and then map the result into a transport DTO.

Architecture rule

Share concepts because two applications truly use them. Do not share them merely because a monorepo makes
imports easy.

lessons.body:
Form Testing, Debugging &
Common Failures
Verify user-visible behavior and diagnose the correct layer

Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Test behavior, not library internals
A form test should prove what the user can do and what the application sends, not whether React Hook
Form happens to store a particular internal property.

Scenario                                        Expected

Submit blank title                              Inline title error; no API request

Enter valid title                               Error clears according to configured validation timing

Double click submit                             One active browser submission; button disabled while pending

API 403                                         Form preserved; permission message shown

API 409                                         Form preserved; conflict message shown

API 500                                         Safe message and requestId surfaced when available

Successful create                               Navigate/refresh to Task list

Successful edit                                 reset accepted values; isDirty becomes false

Debugging order

Is the field registered / controlled?

What are current values/defaultValues?

Did Zod reject the UI shape?

Did handleSubmit run?

Was the request sent?

What HTTP status/error code returned?

Did reset/navigation run after success?

Useful tooling
Use browser DevTools Network for HTTP, React DevTools for component boundaries, and temporary
RHF watch/getValues logging only while diagnosing. Do not ship logs containing sensitive form values.

Common failure: default mismatch
If the form appears dirty immediately, compare the actual initialized values with defaultValues. Empty
string, null and undefined differences are a frequent cause.

Common failure: custom component never blurs
A custom controlled component must forward onChange and onBlur correctly if your validation mode
depends on blur events.

lessons.body:
Hands-On Lab & Phase Exit
Move from tutorial form code to independent form architecture decisions

Phase 21 - Forms with React Hook Form + Zod
Volume 06 - Professional Frontend

Hands-on lab
Implement the complete create/edit Task form flow in the course repository. Do the work in small
checkpoints; do not paste the final reference snapshot first.

Level 1 - Follow
Install the locked packages, create the shared validators package, add the Task form schema, render
accessible title/description/priority/due-date fields, and verify client validation.

Level 2 - Modify
Add a character counter for description that does not replace the server-side maximum-length rule.
Add a clear due-date button that sets the form value to an empty string and maps to null on submit.

Level 3 - Implement
Build the Edit Task page. It must load server data, initialize the form, disable Save while unchanged,
preserve input after a 409 failure, and reset dirty state after a successful save.

Level 4 - Engineer
Design a reusable form architecture for an HRIS leave request with leave type, start/end dates, half-day
option and reason. Identify which rules belong in: shared Zod primitives, web form schema, NestJS
transport validation, service business rules, and PostgreSQL constraints.

Phase exit oral exam
Question                                        You should be able to explain

Why validate twice?                             Browser UX vs untrusted API boundary

Why can form schema differ from DTO?            UI controls and HTTP transport have different shapes

What does isDirty mean?                         Current values differ from current defaults

When use Controller?                            Controlled/custom component needs an adapter

Why preserve values on failure?                 Server rejection should not destroy user work

Why not put form state in TanStack              Form state is local transient editing state
Query?

Graduation checkpoint

Phase 21 is complete when a user can create and edit a Task with accessible validation, secure authenticated
submission, clear pending/error behavior, and the server remains authoritative for validation and business rules.

lessons.body:
Guided Build Lab — Phase 21: Forms with React Hook Form + Zod

Purpose
Build robust forms with React Hook Form and Zod while separating transient form state from authoritative server state.

Deliverable
Create/edit task forms with shared field rules, accessible errors, async submission, server-error mapping, and reset behavior.

Before you touch the code
Open the previous phase checkpoint, run the repository's verification commands, and make sure Git is clean. A guided lab is useful only when you know which change introduced a failure. Write down the current browser/API/database behavior you expect before modifying anything.

Architecture trace
input controls -> React Hook Form state -> Zod resolver -> submit mutation -> API validation/business rules -> field/non-field feedback

Read this flow left to right, then right to left. For each arrow, say what data crosses the boundary, which side trusts the other, and what evidence would prove that this boundary works. This habit prevents framework APIs from becoming disconnected memorization.

Step 1 — Define form values and defaults before wiring UI fields.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Step 2 — Register basic fields and observe dirty/touched/submitting state intentionally.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Step 3 — Connect Zod resolver and reuse only rules that genuinely belong in both client and API validation.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Step 4 — Implement accessible field errors and focus behavior after invalid submit.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Step 5 — Send data through the mutation layer and map server validation/conflict errors back to fields or form-level feedback.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Step 6 — Implement edit/reset/cancel semantics and test what happens when server data changes while a form is open.
Do the smallest version of this step first. After the change, stop and verify it before continuing. Use terminal output, HTTP responses, browser DevTools, tests, or database inspection depending on the boundary. If the result differs from your prediction, do not add more code; explain the mismatch and fix the earliest failing assumption.

Checkpoint
When the lab works, inspect git diff. Remove accidental debugging output and unrelated edits. Run type checking/tests/build commands relevant to this phase. Commit the checkpoint with a message that describes the capability added, not merely the files changed.

Explain-back
Without looking at the lesson, explain why each layer in the architecture trace exists, what this phase added to TaskFlow, and what would break if the new responsibility were moved to the wrong layer. If you cannot explain the boundary, repeat the trace before moving on.

lessons.title: Debugging Workshop
lessons.summary:
Goal
Learn to diagnose this phase's failures systematically instead of reinstalling packages, changing random configuration, or copying a fix without understanding it.
lessons.body:
Debugging Workshop — Phase 21: Forms with React Hook Form + Zod

Goal
Learn to diagnose this phase's failures systematically instead of reinstalling packages, changing random configuration, or copying a fix without understanding it.

The debugging loop
1. Reproduce the failure with the smallest reliable action.
2. Capture the exact symptom: command, status code, stack trace, network request, database state, or UI state.
3. Locate the earliest boundary where actual behavior diverges from expected behavior.
4. Form one hypothesis.
5. Change one variable.
6. Re-run the same reproduction.
7. Keep the fix only if the evidence supports the hypothesis.

Boundary walk
input controls -> React Hook Form state -> Zod resolver -> submit mutation -> API validation/business rules -> field/non-field feedback

Start at the visible symptom and walk backward. Do not debug the database when the browser never sent the request. Do not debug React state when the API is returning a deterministic 403. The boundary walk tells you which evidence to collect next.

Failure drill 1 — Duplicating server data into form state without reset strategy
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Failure drill 2 — Assuming client validation secures the API
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Failure drill 3 — Clearing user input on every failed request
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Failure drill 4 — Showing only generic toast instead of actionable field errors
Create or imagine this failure in a safe development environment. Write the expected symptom first. Then list the two or three observations that would distinguish this failure from neighboring causes. Repair it with the smallest change and verify the original reproduction no longer fails.

Do not hide the evidence
Avoid immediately clearing caches, deleting lockfiles, resetting the database, disabling security checks, or reinstalling everything. Those actions may erase the evidence that teaches you what was wrong. Use them only after you can explain why they are relevant.

Debugging exit ticket
Pick one failure from this workshop and write a short incident note: symptom, scope, root cause, fix, verification, and prevention. This is the same communication pattern used in professional bug reports and production incident follow-ups.

lessons.title: Phase Synthesis & Independent Challenge
lessons.summary:
Mission

lessons.body:
Phase Synthesis & Independent Challenge — Forms with React Hook Form + Zod

Mission
Rebuild the capability of Phase 21 without following the exact code line-by-line. The goal is transfer: can you use the ideas when the variable names, UI, or route shape changes?

Required outcome
Build robust forms with React Hook Form and Zod while separating transient form state from authoritative server state.

Required artifact
Create/edit task forms with shared field rules, accessible errors, async submission, server-error mapping, and reset behavior.

Constraints
• Start from the previous phase checkpoint or a fresh branch.
• Use the course architecture boundaries, but do not copy the reference implementation until after your first attempt.
• Keep changes scoped to the capability.
• Preserve validation, authorization, error handling, and observability expectations already earned in earlier phases.
• Record any design decision where more than one implementation is reasonable.

Acceptance criteria
• Can distinguish form state from server state.
• Can build schema-backed forms.
• Can handle async errors.
• Can reason about create vs edit/reset lifecycles.

Independent build sequence
1. Define form values and defaults before wiring UI fields.
2. Register basic fields and observe dirty/touched/submitting state intentionally.
3. Connect Zod resolver and reuse only rules that genuinely belong in both client and API validation.
4. Implement accessible field errors and focus behavior after invalid submit.
5. Send data through the mutation layer and map server validation/conflict errors back to fields or form-level feedback.
6. Implement edit/reset/cancel semantics and test what happens when server data changes while a form is open.

Self-review
Compare your implementation to the reference only after the acceptance criteria pass. Differences are not automatically mistakes. For each difference, ask: does it preserve the same contract, security boundary, correctness, maintainability, and operational behavior? Keep the alternative when you can justify it with evidence.

Stretch challenge
Change one assumption: more users, a second tenant, a slow network, an expired session, a concurrent mutation, a deployment restart, or a failed dependency. Predict whether your design still behaves correctly. If not, document the next architectural improvement rather than adding complexity blindly.

Phase exit
Run the relevant checks, inspect Git diff, and write a three-sentence summary: what the system can do now, which boundary owns the new responsibility, and which failure you now know how to diagnose. Only then mark the phase complete.

lessons.title: Mastery Capstone Lab
lessons.summary: Integrate Phase 21 without following a transcript.
lessons.body:
Mastery Capstone Lab

This is the transfer exercise for Phase 21: Forms with React Hook Form + Zod. The detailed lessons are now closed-book reference material. Your task is to prove that the phase outcome can be reproduced from requirements, repository evidence, and debugging—not by copying a finished implementation.

Target artifact
Create/edit task forms with shared field rules, accessible errors, async submission, server-error mapping, and reset behavior.

Acceptance criteria
- Write the behavior and constraints before implementation.
- Identify the owning layer and every boundary crossed.
- Implement the smallest complete vertical slice.
- Verify the happy path from outside the implementation.
- Demonstrate at least one expected failure path.
- Run the phase-relevant quality checks.
- Review the diff for accidental duplication, leaked responsibilities, missing validation/authorization, and hidden environment assumptions.

Evidence packet
Save the command/request used, expected result, actual result, one failure reproduction, the fix, and a short explanation of why the final responsibility belongs where it does. This packet is more valuable than a screenshot of a green page because it demonstrates repeatable engineering reasoning.

Stretch
Change one requirement after the first implementation. Measure which files must change. If a tiny domain change causes unrelated layers to move, use that evidence to discuss coupling before adding another abstraction.

references.preview:
# TaskFlow Phase 21 reference snapshot

This snapshot demonstrates the form architecture taught in Phase 21. It is a teaching reference, not a drop-in replacement for earlier phase source files. Integrate the changes deliberately.

The key design is: React Hook Form owns transient form state; Zod validates the client experience; NestJS validates the HTTP request again; business rules remain in services; PostgreSQL remains authoritative persistence.

# Phase 21 form test matrix

- Blank title -> inline error; request not sent.
- Unknown browser-only field -> not included in transport mapping.
- Create success -> navigate/refresh Task list.
- Edit success -> reset accepted values and clear dirty state.
- API 401 -> preserve values and show authentication/recovery message.
- API 403 -> preserve values and show permission message.
- API 409 -> preserve values and show conflict message.
- API 500 -> generic safe message; include requestId when client error helper exposes it.
- Double-click submit -> submit control disabled while isSubmitting is true.
- Keyboard-only -> labels, focus, errors and submit remain operable.
- Mobile width -> fields stack; button remains reachable without horizontal page overflow.
